title: Torque Management Request Input Signal "B" Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the torque management request signal and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. Another module (often the transmission computer) uses this signal to ask the engine to cut power briefly, such as during shifts.

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault between the engine and transmission computers
Network communication problem between modules
Module software that needs an update
Transmission or engine computer fault

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the torque management request signal reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Repair the wiring or network fault, or update the module software as the maker directs.

title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the hood switch and has spotted an electrical fault. The car checks whether the hood is closed, for safety with remote start and engine stop-start.
symptoms: Remote start or stop-start may stop working

causes.name: Hood switch dirty, misadjusted or damaged
Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the hood switch
Broken or chafed wire in the hood switch circuit
Failed hood switch
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the hood switch, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the hood switch.

title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the throttle/fuel inhibit circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. This circuit lets another module tell the engine to limit throttle or fuel, for example for safety or security.
symptoms: Reduced power or engine may not rev
Engine may not start in some cases

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault in the inhibit circuit
Fault in the module that sends the inhibit request
Aftermarket remote start or alarm wired into the circuit
Engine computer fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the throttle/fuel inhibit circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the inhibit circuit wiring or the module sending the signal; remove faulty aftermarket add-ons.

title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the engine coolant level sensor circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. This sensor warns the computer when the coolant reservoir gets low.
symptoms: Low coolant warning may come on or stay on

causes.name: Coolant level actually low
Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the coolant level sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the engine coolant level sensor circuit
Failed coolant level sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: With the engine cold, check the coolant level first
Look over the connector and wiring for the engine coolant level sensor circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the coolant level sensor.

title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance

causes.name: Coolant level actually low
Failing or sticking coolant level sensor
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: With the engine cold, check the coolant level first
Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the engine coolant level sensor circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the coolant level sensor itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

Failed coolant level sensor

checks: With the engine cold, check the coolant level first
Inspect the wiring in the engine coolant level sensor circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Unplug the coolant level sensor and see if the reading changes
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the coolant level sensor.

title: A/C Request "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the A/C request signal and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. This is the signal from the A/C controls asking the engine computer to turn on the compressor.
symptoms: A/C may not turn on or may not shut off
Idle may change when A/C is switched

causes.name: Failing or sticking climate control switch or module
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the A/C request signal reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the climate control switch or module itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Engine Coolant Level Low
plain: The coolant level sensor says the coolant reservoir is low. Low coolant can lead to overheating.
symptoms: Check engine or low coolant warning on

causes.name: Coolant leak from a hose, radiator or water pump
Coolant slowly lost over time
Leaking head gasket
Faulty coolant level sensor

checks: With the engine cold, check the coolant reservoir level
Look for wet spots or dried coolant around hoses and the radiator
Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs
fix: Top up and find the leak; replace the level sensor only if the level is correct.

title: A/C Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
plain: The climate control module found a problem in its own system and asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light.
symptoms: A/C or heater may not work properly

causes.name: Stored fault in the A/C or climate control module
Climate control wiring problem
Climate control module fault

checks: Scan the climate control module for its own codes
Fix those codes first, then clear this one
fix: Repair whatever fault is stored in the climate control module.

title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the turbocharger boost control position sensor and has spotted an electrical fault. It tells the computer where the turbo boost control (vanes or wastegate) is sitting.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the turbocharger boost control position sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the turbocharger boost control position sensor circuit
Failed turbocharger boost control position sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the turbocharger boost control position sensor, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the turbocharger boost control position sensor.

title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The sensor that reports the position of the turbo boost control (usually the variable vanes) is giving readings that do not match what the computer commanded.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Sticking turbo vanes from carbon buildup
Failed turbo actuator or position sensor
Vacuum leak or bad vacuum control valve on vacuum-operated actuators
Wiring or connector fault at the actuator
Worn turbo linkage

checks: Watch commanded versus actual vane position with a scan tool
Check vacuum lines and the boost control valve if the actuator uses vacuum
Check whether the actuator rod moves freely
fix: Often a new turbo actuator or position sensor; sometimes the turbo vanes must be cleaned or the turbo replaced.

cost.job: Replace turbo actuator or position sensor

examples: Well known on Volkswagen and Audi TDI diesels with variable-vane turbos

title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent
plain: The computer is watching the turbocharger boost control position sensor and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. It tells the computer where the turbo boost control (vanes or wastegate) is sitting.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Turbocharger boost control position sensor failing on and off

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the turbocharger boost control position sensor with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the turbocharger boost control position sensor if the wiring is solid.
